summary.oneLiner: The Supreme Court's August 2024 judgment terminated toll collection rights, slashing revenue by ~70%, but the company is filing a review petition to challenge legal findings and preserve its concession agreement; the outcome will determine whether arbitration for ₹2,000+ crore compensation proceeds or the company remains stranded with non-commercializable land assets.

one-line thesis: The Supreme Court's August 2024 judgment terminated toll collection rights, slashing revenue by ~70%, but the company is filing a review petition to challenge legal findings and preserve its concession agreement; the outcome will determine whether arbitration for ₹2,000+ crore compensation proceeds or the company remains stranded with non-commercializable land assets.
financial scorecard: revenue: -68% YoY (₹130cr → ₹42cr); EBITDA/margin: -85% YoY (₹95cr → ₹14cr; margin 73% → 33%); PAT (rptd): -92% YoY (₹78cr → ₹6cr); PAT (normalized): -95% YoY (ex-one-off legal costs); order book: 0 (toll rights suspended); net debt: ₹1,120cr (unchanged; no capex, no repayment)
guidance: revenue growth: none (toll suspended); margin: no guidance (revenue dependent on legal outcome); order inflow: none; capex/commissioning: ₹0 (no new projects; maintenance only)
segment / subsidiary detail: Toll revenue: suspended since Oct 2016; advertising revenue: ₹42cr annually (up 100% from prior low, but at max capacity); land assets: 36 acres along DND Flyway, charged to lenders, possession retained but development rights ungranted
growth verticals / optionality: None; development rights on 36 acres contingent on Supreme Court reversing judgment; no viable alternative revenue streams without legal relief
margins & cost dynamics: Fixed maintenance costs remain unchanged (₹28cr/year); no variable cost reduction possible; advertising revenue capped by concession space; margin compression driven by revenue collapse, not cost inflation
capex / expansion: ₹0 for FY26; no new capex planned; only maintenance expenditure of ₹28cr/year continues
capital allocation: Prioritize legal defense (review petition); no dividends paid since 2016; no buybacks or share issuance planned; cash reserves used solely for legal costs and maintenance
risks & watch-items: Review petition likely to fail (historical SC review success rate <5%); arbitration may be blocked by SC's 'company made money' observation; land assets cannot be monetized without development rights; lenders may enforce charge if covenant breached; reputational risk from public perception of 'government betrayal'
management quality / tone: Defiant but constrained; acknowledges legal defeat but insists on contractual rights; emphasizes review petition as last resort; avoids committing to arbitration timeline; admits revenue is unsustainable without legal reversal
non-obvious takeaways: The company's 36-acre land is legally owned and charged to lenders, but its value is zero without development rights — lenders may have overvalued it as collateral; the CFO is from NTBCL, not NOIDA, contradicting shareholder claims of 'government control'; CAG shortfall of ₹1,900cr is the only quantifiable claim left, but SC's 'adequate compensation' finding may nullify it

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supreme Court's judgment terminated toll rights and dismissed NTBCL's appeal | Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd | loser | High | Stock price has fallen 90% since 2016; no revenue visibility without review success |
| Supreme Court's observation that 'company has made money' undermines arbitration claim | Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd | loser | High | Arbitration for ₹2,000cr+ hinges on overturning this finding |
| NOIDA Authority may face political backlash if forced to pay compensation | NOIDA Authority | beneficiary | Low | Avoids liability if review fails; no immediate financial exposure |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
